answer: Sybil resistance rests on per-identity proof-of-work: every miner must find a nonce whose hash beats the epoch target, so each extra identity is a separate paid search. There is no bridge letting one operator reuse work across thousands of accounts; ten thousand fakes cost ten thousand full searches in electricity and hardware. Honest miners spread over a tundra of real hashing, so a sybil swarm must outspend them while its locked stake earns nothing until it wins. The old fable of free identity collapses when each new key costs as much as genuine block work.
